items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and /or equivalent experience / training.
Experience utilizing critical thinking, analytical and creative problem solving skills for program and financial management/analysis.
Experience assessing college transcripts and accurately calculating course grades and grade point averages, balances and deficiencies.
Experience and/or training on advising/counseling students.

Under general supervision and in collaboration with the faculty Graduate Program Chairs, the Graduate Program Coordinator is responsible for managing all aspects of the assigned graduate programs, designated emphases, graduate certificates, and post-bac certificate programs. Serve as backup for all others. This unit has 5 graduate programs, 5 designated emphases and 1 post-bac certificate. Responsible for providing comprehensive administrative, career, and academic support. Manage graduate funding, including fellowships, employment, and reimbursements. Working closely with graduate program committees, develop strategic plans for instructional programs and marketing/recruitment. Coordinate the hiring of graduate students (all titles) and readers (graduate, undergraduate, non-student). This is a hybrid position.
Mathematical competence to calculate GPAs and employment percentages and to create/follow/monitor budgets.
Working knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.
Knowledge of university, Graduate Council, and graduate program policy/procedure requirements and their application to specific programs of major.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to communicate effectively verbally and in writing.
Knowledge of complex U.S. visa and immigration procedures, compliance issues, and employment eligibility / authorization for international students.
Ability to work with diverse populations with multicultural competence.

Knowledge of University-specific computer application programs and knowledge of University and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.
Ability in problem identification and reasoning; ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Knowledge of the marketing process. Ability to conduct research and compose/present compelling stories.
Skills to obtain, synthesize, and analyze data and develop statistics from a variety of campus sources.
